newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chelyabsvyazinform yet to get new issue permission.
newsitem.headline: Chelyabsvyazinform yet to get new issue permission.

text.p: Russian regional telecom Chelyabsvyazinform is yet to ask permission from majority shareholder Svyazinvest to issue new shares, a top official said on Friday.
"We are preparing to ask Svyazinvest for permission to make a secondary issue and we must now prepare our financial plan," Sergei Akimenko, the company's deputy chief executive, said by telephone.
Akimenko said he had been mistaken when he said on Thursday that Svyazinvest had already agreed in principle to the issue.
State-owned telecoms holding company Svyazinvest has 56.34 percent of voting stock in Svyazinform Chelyabinskoi Oblasti, which is based in the Urals town of Chelyabinsk.
He said new shares could be issued in stages beginning no earlier than next year after a state-held stake was sold and shareholders approved the issue.
Akimenko also said the company, located east of the Urals mountains at the edge of Siberia, planned to register a new issue of domestic bonds this year, but he gave no further details.
Many Russian regional telecoms firms are eager to expand and improve their networks, but they lack funds and have little hope of help from Svyazinvest, a government-owned holding.

Shares in Chelyabsvyazinform, formally known as Svyazinform Chelyabinskoi Oblasti, are traded on the RTS-2 market of relatively illiquid and less traded shares. The company closed at $55.75 on Thursday, when it was last quoted.
